sbvoelklingenhuette.name: Völklingen Ironworks
sbvoelklingenhuette.slogan: Blast furnaces that now glow for visitors instead of for steel.
sbvoelklingenhuette.line: One of the only intact ironworks surviving from the 19th and early-20th centuries in Europe and North America.

sbludwigskirche.name: Ludwigskirche
sbludwigskirche.slogan: Stengel's Baroque jewel, set in a square he designed as one artwork.
sbludwigskirche.line: Built from 1762 to 1775, it was nearly destroyed by bombs in 1944 and its rebuilding began in 1949.

sbschlossberghoehlen.name: Homburg Schlossberg Caves
sbschlossberghoehlen.slogan: Twelve levels of hand-cut red sandstone beneath Homburg.
sbschlossberghoehlen.line: Dug from soft red sandstone, the caves run to about 5,000 m of tunnels and sheltered Homburg's people in the Second World War.

sbsaarlouismarkt.name: Saarlouis Old Town
sbsaarlouismarkt.slogan: Louis XIV's star-shaped fortress town, still laid out by Vauban.
sbsaarlouismarkt.line: Founded in 1680 on the orders of Louis XIV, it was designed by Vauban, and Marshal Ney was born here.

sbschloss.name: Saarbrücken Palace
sbschloss.slogan: A Baroque palace wearing a modern steel-and-glass heart.
sbschloss.line: Stengel finished the Baroque palace in 1748; a steel-skeleton central pavilion by Gottfried Böhm's team followed in 1989.
